You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From eaa2f87c6b840b83827c40db6eb8481689570259 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Aug 2017 13:30:30 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] x86/ldt: Fix off by one in get_segment_base()

ldt->entries[] is allocated in alloc_ldt_struct().  It has
ldt->nr_entries elements and ldt->nr_entries is capped at LDT_ENTRIES.
So if "idx" is == ldt->nr_entries then we're reading beyond the end of
the buffer.  It seems duplicative to have two limit checks when one
would work just as well so I removed the check against LDT_ENTRIES.

The gdt_page.gdt[] array has GDT_ENTRIES entries.

Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Acked-by: Andy Lutomirski <luto@kernel.org>
Cc: Alexander Shishkin <alexander.shishkin@linux.intel.com>
Cc: Arnaldo Carvalho de Melo <acme@kernel.org>
Cc: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Cc: kernel-janitors@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: d07bdfd322d3 ("perf/x86: Fix USER/KERNEL tagging of samples properly")
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/20170818102516.gqwm4xdvvuvjw5ho@mwanda
Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>

diff --git a/arch/x86/events/core.c b/arch/x86/events/core.c
index af12e294caed..939050169d12 100644
--- a/arch/x86/events/core.c
+++ b/arch/x86/events/core.c
@@ -2335,12 +2335,9 @@ static unsigned long get_segment_base(unsigned int segment)
 #ifdef CONFIG_MODIFY_LDT_SYSCALL
 		struct ldt_struct *ldt;
 
-		if (idx > LDT_ENTRIES)
-			return 0;
-
 		/* IRQs are off, so this synchronizes with smp_store_release */
 		ldt = lockless_dereference(current->active_mm->context.ldt);
-		if (!ldt || idx > ldt->nr_entries)
+		if (!ldt || idx >= ldt->nr_entries)
 			return 0;
 
 		desc = &ldt->entries[idx];
@@ -2348,7 +2345,7 @@ static unsigned long get_segment_base(unsigned int segment)
 		return 0;
 #endif
 	} else {
-		if (idx > GDT_ENTRIES)
+		if (idx >= GDT_ENTRIES)
 			return 0;
 
 		desc = raw_cpu_ptr(gdt_page.gdt) + idx;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/events/core.c`**
   - The condition checking if `idx` is greater than `LDT_ENTRIES` has been removed.
   - The condition checking if `idx` is greater than `ldt->nr_entries` has been modified to check if `idx` is greater than or equal to `ldt->nr_entries`.
   - Similarly, the condition checking if `idx` is greater than `GDT_ENTRIES` has been modified to check if `idx` is greater than or equal to `GDT_ENTRIES`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in the file are related to fixing an off-by-one error in the `get_segment_base()` function. By changing the conditions to use "greater than or equal to" instead of "greater than," the patch ensures that the function does not attempt to access an out-of-bounds index in the `ldt->entries` and `gdt_page.gdt` arrays. This change simplifies the logic by removing redundant checks and ensures that the function behaves correctly when accessing these arrays, thus preventing potential memory access violations.

2. output the file name that is most likely to cause the bug.
